title: When the computer's disk is full
summary: Confirm it's the computer (not the backup stick), free room or move the house folder, then retry.

start.body: Photos won't copy, the share says no space, or df shows the system disk packed. Don't buy a NAS because one small SSD filled up.

df.body: SSH in. Run df -h. Point at the line that ends in /. 95–100% Use% (or tiny Avail) means the computer itself is the problem. House folder already on a stay-in USB? Also: df -h /srv/share.

choices.label: Bytes free but copies still fail
Only the backup stick is full

inodes.body: Check file slots: df -i /. If IUse% is near 100%, you ran out of inodes (lots of tiny files), not gigabytes. Fix that before buying a bigger drive.

backup-stick.body: Wrong page for a /mnt/backup stick you unplug. Free or replace that stick — don't wipe the live share to make the backup fit.

full-root.body: See what's eating space: sudo du -sh /srv/share and sudo du -h --max-depth=1 / 2>/dev/null | sort -h. Clear apt leftovers and old logs if that's the bulk. Don't delete /srv/share without a trusted second copy.

choices.label: House folder is huge; SSD is small

clear.body: Clear old package downloads and old logs. Empty Trash/Downloads you don't need. Re-check df -h /. Leave headroom so next week's photos don't fail.

usb-park.body: Park the live share on a USB disk that stays plugged in. Same share name for phones and laptops. Keep a second copy elsewhere first.
